summary: @servicetitan/component-usage 28.5.5 ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun and executes an obfuscated payload
details: The package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/`, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a 727KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle with a rotated string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shifts a ~1000-entry atom array) and mangled identifiers; no plaintext URLs are visible and endpoints are reconstructed at runtime. setup.mjs itself uses javascript-obfuscator-style hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`,...) and property-indirection tables, and ships a hand-rolled ZIP central-directory parser (`xn`) as a fallback to system unzip so the dropper runs regardless of installed tooling. package.json `files` declares only `bin`, `dist`, `src`, `static`; dist/index.js is a legitimate DataDog metrics/component-usage library that never references setup.mjs or math_init.js. The dropper files sit at tarball root outside the publisher's declared library surface, consistent with a compromised-publish where a preinstall stage was grafted onto an otherwise-normal ServiceTitan library. Fetching the Bun runtime specifically routes execution around Node-based install-time inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
